english.title: Smoke electronic cigarette or other like device on the railway - railway bye-law
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) smoked an electronic cigarette or other like device namely, **(..SPECIFY DEVICE..) on a part of the railway where there was a notice indicating that smoking was not allowed
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaws 3(2) and 24 of the Railway Byelaws.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)

english.notes:
(i) Byelaw 24(2) provides a power for authorised person to remove persons from the railway. See Byelaw 23(1) for the associated power to require a name and address.
(ii) Schedule 2 to the Railway Byelaws provides that in byelaw 25(1) the following operators are excluded from the definition of operator; Great Central Railway (Nottingham) Limited, London Underground Limited Tube Lines Limited and Tyne and Wear Passenger Transport Executive.
(iii) The Railway Byelaws 2005 were made by the Strategic Rail Authority under section 219 of the Transport Act 2000 and confirmed under Schedule 20 to the Transport Act 2000, both of which were repealed on 15th October 2015. Section 46(4) of the Railways Act 2005 provides that these Byelaws remain in force.
